_comment: Baseline for the nightly 8-GPU MXFP4 gate. Only mean_tflops_per_device and
mean_loss are read by ci/perf/parse_perf_log.py; every other key is
provenance for whoever has to decide whether a red night is real.
PROVISIONAL. This value came from a SOURCE build in the dev image on
smci355-ccs-aus-m15-29. The nightly measures the shipped WHEEL on a
linux-jax-aiter-mi355-8 runner, which is an org-managed ARC ephemeral
pool, NOT the fixed host n15-13 an earlier version of this note named. So
two things differ from the number below and neither is pinned down:
packaging, and which node of that pool the night lands on. Leave
`gate: false` until several nights are on record, then replace the numbers
below with the median of those nights and turn the gate on.
2026-08-31, the packaging half, measured: the +full wheel was run on
m15-29 -- the SAME host as the 1840.6644 source figure -- and landed at
1822.2915 (tail 40-49, mean 2.0824 s), -1.00%. N=1 on both sides. Note
this is NOT a dev-vs-manylinux clang comparison: the wheel's attention
libs (librmsnorm_fwd, libmha_fwd, libmha_bwd) are built in the dev image
and only packaged by manylinux, so both sides carry the same attention
objects. Related: areas/analysis.md records an rv_release (dev-image)
wheel at 1827.3868, -0.72%. The node-to-node half is still unmeasured --
the nightly perf leg has not yet completed a green run.
Do NOT compare a ci_regression (FSDP4, batch 4, global 16) number against
this file. That profile's own baseline is ~1784.68 and reading it against
1840 shows a 3% regression that does not exist.
label: 8b_fp4_fsdp8

provenance.note: Frozen blog MXFP4 figure. Three further source runs of the same recipe gave 1837.1388 / 1838.1214 / 1840.0823 (mean 1839.00, sd 0.09%), so run-to-run spread on a quiet box is well under the 5% gate threshold.
